hardware: Linux VM (aarch64, 4 vCPU) on Apple Silicon Mac. CPU only, single process.
implementation: Pure NumPy + PIL. No GPU, no PyTorch, no compiled extensions.
measured: Wall clock per keyframe, mean of 10 consecutive keyframes, 10 LiDAR sweeps each (~266k returns).
optimisation: Scatter-add for ray carving moved from np.add.at to np.bincount on flattened indices. np.add.at is the documented slow unbuffered path. Not bit-identical: float32 accumulation order moves a few cells by at most one free unit (0.45 log-odds) across the gap-fill threshold, but the tri-state classification is unchanged (0 of 291,600 cells differ), so no downstream decision moves.
caveat: Unoptimised reference implementation on a virtualised CPU. Not a real-time claim; no GPU or C++ path was benchmarked.
